title: BattleScribe Spec Protocol
description: Schema for the NDJSON wire protocol between spec runner and engine adapters. Each line is either a command (runner → adapter) or a response (adapter → runner), discriminated by the "type" property.

command.description: A message sent from the spec runner to the engine adapter.

response.description: A message sent from the engine adapter to the spec runner.

corrId.description: Optional correlation id (protocol v1.1+); adapters echo it verbatim on the response. Distinct from any domain-specific "id" field on this message.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C trace-context header (protocol v1.1+). Lets the adapter parent its spans under the client's span. Per-request, not per-process: one adapter process serves many specs.

tracestate.description: Optional W3C tracestate, companion to traceparent. Together they form a trace-context carrier an adapter can feed to its stock propagator.

selections.description: Map of entryId → the selection node ids the action minted from that entry, in roster order. A list, not a single id: one action routinely creates two selections of one entry (a min=2 auto-add), and reporting one of them leaves the other unnameable. Index 0 is what ${{ steps.X.selections.<entryId> }} resolves to.

categories.description: Map of categoryEntryId → the category node ids the created force owns, in force order. Returned by addForce, addChildForce and duplicateForce; duplicateForce returns the copy's own nodes, which are freshly minted. A list for the same reason selections is one: a force entry can link one category entry twice.

adapterCapabilities.description: Protocol v1.1: optional capabilities advertised by describeResult.

id.description: Runtime node id of the category. Present for a FORCE's categories, which are roster nodes; a SELECTION's categories are the tags it counts against and may have no node identity (they do not on NewRecruit). Distinct from entryId, which several nodes can share.
